text: Lleu, called Llaw Gyffes, is a hero of Welsh legend. His name appears in four of the triads. One of these portrays him as a warrior. He is the son of Arianrhod and a grandson of Dôn. His uncle Gwydion raises him with craft and magic. Math also plays a part in the boy's shaping. A poem in Llyfr Taliesin supports the warrior view. Folk remembered that his grave lay beneath the sea. That grave sat near the resting place of a kinsman. Lleu's tale weaves prophecy, trickery, and a strange death by betrayal.
